# DataSurgeon

DataSurgeon (ds) is a versatile tool for extracting sensitive data and patterns from text and files. It can identify emails, phone numbers, hashes, credit cards, URLs, IP addresses, MAC addresses, DNS records, and more.

Key features:

- Cross-platform usage (Windows, Linux, macOS)
- Recursive directory analysis
- Plugin support (runtime plugin usage may be available)
- CSV output for easy processing

Usage examples:

- Extract files listed on a webpage and deduplicate results:

  $ wget -qO - https://www.example.com | ds -F --clean | uniq

- Search a directory recursively and display filename and line number:

  $ ds --directory test_dir/ -Dl

- Output results to CSV:

  $ wget -qO - https://www.example.com | ds -o output.csv -C

Examples above demonstrate typical command-line usage. For help with available command-line options, run:

  $ ds --help

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from harness import run
import pathlib, json, subprocess, os
home="/tmp/fh1"
def set_plugin(regex, arg="plug", ctype="plugtype"):
    plugin=[{"arg_long_name":arg,"help_message":"h","content_type":ctype,"source_url":"http://x","version":"1","regex":regex}]
    pathlib.Path(f"{home}/.DataSurgeon/plugins.json").write_text(json.dumps(plugin))
def do(regex, inp, args=["-S","-C","--plug"]):
    set_plugin(regex)
    p=run(args, inp+"\n")
    print(f"regex={regex!r} inp={inp!r} args={args} => out={p.stdout!r} err={p.stderr!r} code={p.returncode}")
do(r"FOO([0-9]+)BAR", "xx FOO123BAR yy")
do(r"(FOO)([0-9]+)", "xx FOO123 yy")
do(r"FOO[0-9]+", "xx FOO123 yy")
do(r"^FOO[0-9]+", "FOO123 yy")
do(r"^FOO[0-9]+", "xx FOO123 yy")
do(r"FOO[0-9]+|BAR[0-9]+", "xx BAR99 yy FOO11")
do(r"(?P<name>FOO[0-9]+)", "xx FOO123 yy")
do(r"FOO[0-9]*", "xx FOO yy")  # empty?
do(r"[invalid", "xx FOO yy")
do(r"(?i)foo[0-9]+", "xx FOO123 yy")
do(r"foo(?=bar)", "xx foobar yy")  # lookahead - regex crate doesn't support, fancy-regex does
do(r"(?<=x)FOO", "xFOO y")
# restore empty
pathlib.Path(f"{home}/.DataSurgeon/plugins.json").write_text("[]")
PY"}

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from harness import run
import os, pathlib, shutil
root="/tmp/walktest2"
shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)
os.makedirs(root)
pathlib.Path(root+"/first.txt").write_text("first@x.com\n")
os.makedirs(root+"/middir")
pathlib.Path(root+"/middir/inner.txt").write_text("inner@x.com\n")
pathlib.Path(root+"/last.txt").write_text("last@x.com\n")
# check actual directory order via python os.scandir (unsorted)
print("scandir root:", [e.name for e in os.scandir(root)])
p=run(["--directory",root,"-e","-D","-C"],"")
print(p.stdout)
# Also check directories themselves as entries: if WalkDir includes dir entries, code presumably filters is_file. When --directory points to a file, WalkDir yields file entry.
# What about FIFOs etc later
# Test permission denied dir
os.makedirs(root+"/noperm")
pathlib.Path(root+"/noperm/secret.txt").write_text("secret@x.com\n")
os.chmod(root+"/noperm", 0o000)
p=run(["--directory",root,"-e","-D","-C"],"")
print("with noperm dir (running as agent? whoami)", repr(p.stdout), p.returncode, repr(p.stderr))
os.chmod(root+"/noperm", 0o755)
# unreadable file
pathlib.Path(root+"/noperm/secret.txt").chmod(0o000)
p=run(["--directory",root,"-e","-D","-C"],"")
print("unreadable file", repr(p.stdout), p.returncode)
pathlib.Path(root+"/noperm/secret.txt").chmod(0o644)
# file unreadable via -f
pathlib.Path(root+"/noperm/secret.txt").chmod(0o000)
p=run(["-f",root+"/noperm/secret.txt","-e"],"")
print("-f unreadable", repr(p.stdout), p.returncode, repr(p.stderr))
PY
id; whoami; ls -ld /tmp/walktest2/noperm

import itertools, string, subprocess, os, pathlib, time
chars=string.ascii_lowercase+string.digits
for L in (4,5):
    inp_path=f"/tmp/extcand{L}.txt"; out_path=f"/tmp/extout{L}.txt"
    if L==5:
        # 60M alphanumeric too large; only letters for length5 first (11.8M lines maybe heavy)
        chars_use=string.ascii_lowercase
    else:
        chars_use=chars
    start=time.time()
    with open(inp_path,"w") as f:
        for i, tup in enumerate(itertools.product(chars_use, repeat=L)):
            f.write(f"f{i:08d}q.{''.join(tup)}\n")
    print(L,"gen time",time.time()-start,"size",pathlib.Path(inp_path).stat().st_size, flush=True)
    start=time.time(); env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]="/tmp/fh1"
    with open(out_path,"wb") as out:
        p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-f",inp_path,"-C","-F"], stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, timeout=120)
    print(L,"run",time.time()-start,p.returncode,pathlib.Path(out_path).stat().st_size, flush=True)
    cand={}
    for i,tup in enumerate(itertools.product(chars_use,repeat=L)): cand[i]=''.join(tup)
    new=[]
    outputs=set()
    count=0
    for line in pathlib.Path(out_path).read_text().splitlines():

        data=line.split(": ",1)[1]; base,_,ext=data.partition("."); idx=int(base[1:-1])
        outputs.add(ext)
        if ext==cand[idx]: new.append(ext)
    print(L,"total hits",count,"exact new",sorted(new),"output exts len=L",sorted([e for e in outputs if len(e)==L]))

{"command":"python3 << 'PY'
import subprocess,os,pathlib,json,shutil
home="/tmp/prhome"; shutil.rmtree(home,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(home+"/.DataSurgeon"); pf=pathlib.Path(home+"/.DataSurgeon/plugins.json")
def plugin(name,url,ver="1"): return {"arg_long_name":name,"help_message":f"h{name}","content_type":f"t{name}","source_url":url,"version":ver,"regex":"X"}
def run(label, plugins, argurl, inp=b""):
 pf.write_text(json.dumps(plugins,indent=2) if plugins is not None else "bad") if plugins is not None else pf.write_text("bad")
 env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
 p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--remove",argurl],input=inp,capture_output=True,env=env,timeout=3)
 print(label,"code",p.returncode,"out",p.stdout[:700],"err",p.stderr[:300],"file",pf.read_text()[:700])
plugins=[plugin("a","https://github.com/foo/repo"),plugin("b","https://github.com/foo/repo"),plugin("c","http://example.com/other"),plugin("d","https://github.com/foo/repo/")]
run("remove exact github no slash",plugins,"https://github.com/foo/repo")
run("remove input slash vs stored no",plugins,"https://github.com/foo/repo/")
run("remove stored slash only",plugins,"https://github.com/foo/repo/")
run("remove nonexistent",plugins,"https://github.com/nope/nope")
run("remove arg name instead",plugins,"a")
run("remove raw github",plugins,"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/foo/repo")
run("remove empty plugins",[],"https://github.com/foo/repo")
run("remove all matches if one plugin",[plugin("a","u")],"u")
run("remove partial url substring",plugins,"github.com/foo/repo")
run("remove case diff",plugins,"HTTPS://github.com/foo/repo")
# missing plugins file
pf.unlink()
env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--remove","x"],input=b"",capture_output=True,env=env)
print("missing",p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr,pf.exists())
# invalid plugins with n n
pf.write_text("bad")
p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--remove","x"],input=b"n\nn\n",capture_output=True,env=env)
print("invalid",p.returncode,p.stdout[:500],p.stderr[:200],pf.read_text())
# read-only file remove existing
pf.write_text(json.dumps(plugins)); pf.chmod(0o444)
p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--remove","https://github.com/foo/repo"],input=b"",capture_output=True,env=env)
print("readonly",p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr,pf.read_text()[:300]); pf.chmod(0o644)
PY"}

{"command":"python3 << 'PY'
import subprocess,os,pathlib,json,collections
home="/tmp/pbad"; pf=pathlib.Path(home+"/.DataSurgeon/plugins.json")
pf.write_text(json.dumps([{"arg_long_name":"email","help_message":"PLUG","content_type":"PLUGTYPE","source_url":"u","version":"1","regex":"XTEST"}]))
env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
def out(args,inp=b"a@b.co XTEST\n",n=10):
 c=collections.Counter()
 for i in range(n):
  p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,env=env); c[p.stdout.decode()]+=1
 print(args,dict(c))
out(["-S","--email"])
out(["-S","-e"])
out(["-S","-C","-T","--email"])
out(["-S","-C","-T","-e"])
out(["-S","-C","-T"])
# plugin named file duplicates builtin - if plugin arg ID distinct, --file value won't set plugin flag
pf.write_text(json.dumps([{"arg_long_name":"file","help_message":"PLUG","content_type":"PLUGTYPE","source_url":"u","version":"1","regex":"XTEST"}]))
out(["-S","-C","-T","-f","/tmp/testdir/a.txt"], b"", n=3)
# stdin with --file nonexist already file error, plugin not selected as a bool flag because builtin takes value
# Plugin named clean: --clean builtin bool; does it select plugin? Input XTEST no email etc and flags -C alone would give all extractors default anyway, -e -C if plugin selected via -C could show plugin
pf.write_text(json.dumps([{"arg_long_name":"clean","help_message":"PLUG","content_type":"PLUGTYPE","source_url":"u","version":"1","regex":"XTEST"}]))
out(["-S","-C","-T","-e"],b"XTEST a@b.co\n")
out(["-S","-T","-e"],b"XTEST a@b.co\n")
# plugin named list and --list flag etc plugin flag bool trigger list branch first so irrelevant
PY"}

REF="/workspace/executable"; NEW="/tmp/ours/executable"
def setup(base):
 shutil.rmtree(base,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(base+"/home/.DataSurgeon"); pathlib.Path(base+"/home/.DataSurgeon/plugins.json").write_text("[]")
 os.makedirs(base+"/data/sub")
 pathlib.Path(base+"/data/a.txt").write_text("hello a@b.co\nno\nsecond 1.2.3.4 c@d.co\n")
 pathlib.Path(base+"/data/sub/b.log").write_text("x@y.co\n")
 pathlib.Path(base+"/data/empty").write_text("")
 return base+"/home"
def run(exe,args,home,cwd,inp=b""):
 env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
 return subprocess.run([exe]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,env=env,cwd=cwd,timeout=5)
def compare(args_fn,label,inp=b""):
 # args_fn takes base and returns args with paths under base; stdout will contain base path differing (/tmp/refcase vs /tmp/newcase) so replace base string in outputs
 ra="/tmp/refcase"; na="/tmp/newcase"; rh=setup(ra); nh=setup(na)
 a=run(REF,args_fn(ra),rh,ra,inp); b=run(NEW,args_fn(na),nh,na,inp)
 aout=a.stdout.replace(ra.encode(),b"BASE"); bout=b.stdout.replace(na.encode(),b"BASE"); aerr=a.stderr.replace(ra.encode(),b"BASE"); berr=b.stderr.replace(na.encode(),b"BASE")
 # collect output files under each base other than input/home maybe compare relative file contents list
 def files(base):
  out={}
  for p in pathlib.Path(base).rglob("*"):
   if p.is_file() and "home" not in p.parts:
    out[str(p.relative_to(base))]=p.read_bytes().replace(base.encode(),b"BASE")
  return out
 fa,fb=files(ra),files(na)
 ok=a.returncode==b.returncode and aout==bout and aerr==berr and fa==fb
 print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL",label)
 if not ok: print(" ref",a.returncode,aout,aerr,fa,"\n new",b.returncode,bout,berr,fb)
 return ok

 h=(b"Location: "+loc+b"\r\n" if loc else b"")+b"Content-Length: 2\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n[]"; return b"HTTP/1.1 "+status+b"\r\n"+h
for label,urltpl,resps in [
 ("userinfo in initial","http://user:pass@127.0.0.1:{}/repo",[resp(b"/final"),resp(None,b"200 OK")]),

 ("query first","http://127.0.0.1:{}/repo?x=1",[resp(b"/final"),resp(None,b"200 OK")]),
 ("cross host second localhost","http://127.0.0.1:{}/repo",[resp(b"http://localhost:{}/final"),resp(None,b"200 OK")]),
]:
 srv=Raw([])
 # patch responses for cross host port placeholder second format later - Raw port known after creation but responses require port: recreate specific below manually for cross? We'll just print for first 3
 srv.responses=list(resps); home="/tmp/referhome"; shutil.rmtree(home,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(home+"/.DataSurgeon"); pathlib.Path(home+"/.DataSurgeon/plugins.json").write_text("[]")
 env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home; url=urltpl.format(srv.port)
 if label.startswith("cross"): srv.responses=[resp(f"http://localhost:{srv.port}/final".encode()),resp(None,b"200 OK")]
 p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--add",url],input=b"",capture_output=True,env=env,timeout=5)
 print(label,p.stdout,p.stderr); [print(r.decode()) for r in srv.reqs]
 srv.sock.close()
